subject: Urgent: elevated latency & errors after v3.1-quant deploy (Auralytics)
messages:
Message 1 (original customer report)
From: Suneet Rao <suneet@auralytics.com>
To: david_kim
Cc: Maya Patel <maya@auralytics.com>, Auralytics Support <support@auralytics.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2027 08:14:22 -0700
Subject: High p95 and 5xx after v3.1-quant deploy — urgent

David —

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95 latency and a burst of 5xx errors at ~02:30 UTC after your team rolled v3.1-quant into our production pool. Throughput dropped ~28% for our hotpaths and several customer-facing endpoints started timing out. This is hitting our checkout flow and causing failed transactions.

Attached is a perf snapshot from 02:00–03:30 UTC (perf_snapshot_2027-10-01.csv) and a quick CPU flame from the time window (cpu_profile_oct01.png). Key metrics: p95 increased from 210ms to 780ms, 5xx rose from 0.2% to 4.7%, and successful token throughput decreased ~30%.

We need an immediate plan: either rollback to the previous serving profile, route our traffic off the new qprofile, or apply a hotfix. Our legal/ops team is watching — if this persists another 6 hours it becomes a formal outage. Please advise ASAP and escalate to your leadership.

Thanks,
Suneet Rao
Head of Platform Operations
Auralytics

Message 2 (acknowledgement + internal loop-in)
From: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Suneet Rao <suneet@auralytics.com>, Auralytics Support <support@auralytics.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra, marissa_cole
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2027 08:41:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p95 and 5xx after v3.1-quant deploy — urgent

Suneet —

Thank you for the data and quick heads-up. I’m very sorry — this is unacceptable. I’ve looped in Rishi (serving/runtime) and Marissa (customer success) to coordinate a response.

Immediate actions I’ve kicked off:
- Marking Auralytics traffic for emergency observation and rate-limiting noisy paths.
- Spun up a dedicated canary pool using v3.0 non-quant for a controlled rollback test.
- Requested full logs (trace IDs) from your team for 02:15–03:45 UTC.

Rishi / Marissa — can you confirm the fastest path: rollback the qprofile, move Auralytics to v3.0 dedicated pool, or apply a quick KV cache adjustment? I’ll standby for recommendation.

I’ll provide a customer-facing timeline in 30 minutes.

— David
David Kim

Redwood Inference

Message 3 (internal technical assessment & mitigation plan)
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: david_kim
Cc: marissa_cole
Date: Sat, 2 Oct 2027 09:40:15 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p95 and 5xx after v3.1-quant deploy — urgent

David —

Quick triage from the runtime team after looking at the snapshots and initial traces:
- Root cause: under v3.1-quant the KV cache hit rate for Auralytics hot sessions drops significantly (observed 18% -> 6%), causing increased autoregressive compute and long tail kernel swaps on the hosting fleet.
- Secondary: the quantization schedule introduced a new token-level memcpy path that stalls under our larger batch sizes; this amplifies p95 on the hotpath.

Short-term mitigations (can do in <30m):
1) Move Auralytics traffic to the v3.0-nonquant dedicated pool we already have warm (immediate rollback-by-routing).
2) Reduce batch window for Auralytics routes to 10ms and lower max_batch to 8 to avoid the memcpy stall.
3) Temporary KV TTL bump to improve hits for hot sessions.

Recommended next steps: implement (1) + (2) now, observe for 1 hour, then decide whether to fully rollback the qprofile or push a micro-patch to the memcpy path.

I’ll open the emergency runbook play (link below) and start the canary move. If we can’t get metrics back within 60–90 minutes, I recommend escalating to exec for a formal rollback / credit discussion.

Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/rollback-runbook
Attached: cpu_profile_oct01.png

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Lead — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

---
Message 4 (customer update + exec loop)
From: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Suneet Rao <suneet@auralytics.com>, Maya Patel <maya@auralytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole, aditya_rao
Date: Sat, 2 Oct 2027 16:38:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p95 and 5xx after v3.1-quant deploy — urgent

Suneet / Maya —

Update from our mitigation: we have moved Auralytics traffic to the v3.0-nonquant dedicated pool and reduced batch sizing for your routes. Early indicators: p95 dropped from ~780ms to ~230ms, 5xx rates returned to baseline (0.3%) and throughput recovered to ~97% of pre-deploy levels. We’ll keep the routing in place until we complete a deeper root-cause patch.

Next steps and ask:
- We plan to keep the v3.0 routing for up to 24 hours while we instrument a micro-patch for the memcpy path. If you approve a full rollback of the qprofile for your account, we can formalize that and provide post-rollback credits per our SLA if applicable.
- We will share a full RCA and timeline by EOD PST today.
- Marissa will reach out on contracting/credit options if you elect rollback.

I have also looped in Aditya (CTO) to ensure exec visibility — if the customer is not satisfied with the mitigation within 6 hours we will bring this to the exec incident bridge for approval of broader rollbacks and credits.

We deeply regret the impact and are treating this as a P1. Thank you for the quick signal and the perf artifacts — they were instrumental.

— David
David Kim
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Cc: Marissa Cole — VP Customer Success (marissa_cole@redwood.ai)
Cc: Aditya Rao — CTO (aditya_rao@redwood.ai)
